MONTRÉAL--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nouveau Monde Graphite Inc. (“NMG” or the “Company”) (NYSE: NMG, TSX: NOU) announces that it received a written notification (the “Notification Letter”) from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) on November 18, 2026, indicating that the Company is not in compliance with Section 802.01C of the NYSE Listed Company Manual because the average closing price of its common shares (the “Shares”) was less than US$1.00 per Share over a consecutive 30 trading-day period.

The Company’s operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter. In addition, it has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Shares, which will continue to trade on the NYSE under the symbol “NMG”, subject to the Company’s compliance with the NYSE’s other continued listing standards. The Shares are also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the Notification Letter does not affect the Company’s compliance status with this listing.

Under Section 802.01C of the NYSE Listed Company Manual, the Company has six months following receipt of the Notification Letter to regain compliance. The Company will regain compliance if, on the last trading day of any calendar month during the six-month cure period, the Shares have a closing price of at least US$1.00 and an average closing price of at least US$1.00 over the 30 trading days preceding the end of that month.

At the end of the six-month cure period, if the Share price has not met the requirement under Section 802.01C of the NYSE Listed Company Manual, the Shares will be subject to NYSE suspension and delisting procedures.

The Company is evaluating available options in response to this Notification Letter.

About Nouveau Monde Graphite

Nouveau Monde Graphite is an integrated company developing responsible mining and advanced processing operations to supply the global economy with carbon-neutral advanced graphite materials. The Company is developing in Québec, Canada, a fully integrated ore-to-processed-graphite value chain to serve tomorrow’s industries in energy, advanced technology, and manufacturing. With recognized ESG standards and structuring partnerships with major customers, NMG is set to become a strategic supplier of advanced materials to leading specialized manufacturers while promoting sustainability, innovation, and supply chain traceability. www.NMG.com.

PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Wabtec Corporation (NYSE: WAB) today announced the appointment of Rich J. Freeland to its Board of Directors, effective Monday, November 23rd.

Wabtec Corporation Appoints Rich J. Freeland to the Board of Directors

Freeland (69) brings more than 40 years of global industrial and operational leadership experience. He most recently served as President and Chief Operating Officer of Cummins Inc., where he helped drive the company’s growth, global expansion, operational excellence, and technology leadership across multiple business segments. During his tenure at Cummins, Freeland held a series of senior executive positions overseeing global operations, manufacturing, distribution, and business growth. He served as President and Chief Operating Officer from 2014 until his retirement in 2019.

"Rich brings a unique combination of large-scale industrial operating experience and board leadership expertise,” said Wabtec Chairman and CEO Rafael Santana. “His proven track record of driving growth, overseeing global operations, developing talent, and guiding companies through periods of market and technology-driven transformation will further strengthen Wabtec's Board as the company executes its long-term strategy."

During his career at Cummins, Freeland held several senior executive leadership positions, including President of the company’s Engine Business, before assuming responsibility for its worldwide operations as President and Chief Operating Officer. Under his leadership, the Engine Business delivered nearly 40% revenue growth, introduced a record number of new products, and expanded global partnerships. As President and COO, he oversaw the company’s global operations and international expansion, helping deliver top-quartile shareholder returns.

Freeland currently serves as Chair of the Board of Directors of Valvoline Inc. and as a director of Cooper-Standard Holdings Inc., where he chairs the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, and Hyliion Holdings Corp. He previously served on the boards of Cummins and Sauer-Danfoss. Freeland holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Industrial Management from Purdue University and a Master of Business Administration from Indiana University.

About Wabtec

Wabtec Corporation (NYSE: WAB) is revolutionizing the way the world moves for future generations. The company is a leading global provider of equipment, systems, digital solutions and value-added services for the freight and transit rail industries, as well as the mining, marine and industrial markets. Wabtec has been a leader in the rail industry for over 150 years and is the worldwide leader in the decarbonization of freight rail. Visit Wabtec’s website at www.wabteccorp.com.

WINDSOR, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--SS&C Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SSNC) today announced the SS&C GlobeOp Forward Redemption Indicator for November 2026 measured 2.31%, up from 1.62% in October.

Asset retention continues to trend favorably heading into year-end.”

The SS&C GlobeOp Forward Redemption Indicator represents the sum of forward redemption notices received from investors in hedge funds administered by SS&C GlobeOp on the SS&C GlobeOp platform, divided by the AuA at the beginning of the month for SS&C GlobeOp fund administration clients on the SS&C GlobeOp platform. Forward redemptions as a percentage of SS&C GlobeOp's assets under administration on the SS&C GlobeOp platform have trended significantly lower since reaching a high of 19.27% in November 2008. The next publication date is December 21, 2026.

Published on the 15th business day of the month, the SS&C GlobeOp Forward Redemption Indicator presents a timely and accurate view of the redemption pipeline for investors in hedge funds on the SS&C GlobeOp administration platform. Movements in the Indicator reflect investor confidence in their allocations to hedge funds. Indicator data is based on actual investor redemption notifications received. The EXTEND study is the first clinical trial to evaluate xenotransplantation of a porcine thymokidney in a patient with end-stage renal disease (ESRD)

EXTEND is the second clinical trial in United Therapeutics’ xeno-organ manufacturing program

SILVER SPRING, Md. & RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, N.C.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--United Therapeutics Corporation (Nasdaq: UTHR), a public benefit corporation, today announced the first clinical xenotransplant in its EXTEND study of the UThymoKidney™ in patients with ESRD. The transplant operation was performed at NYU Langone Health.

The ongoing EXTEND study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of the UThymoKidney in ESRD patients who are not eligible for conventional allogeneic kidney transplantation or who are on an Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) kidney transplant waitlist, but are more likely to die or go untransplanted within five years than receive a kidney transplant.

United Therapeutics’ investigational UThymoKidney is a xenokidney that contains porcine thymic tissue and is derived from a pig with a single gene edit. The pig’s thymus tissue is intended to condition the recipient’s immune system to recognize the UThymoKidney as “self” and reduce the likelihood of organ rejection. The single gene responsible for the synthesis of alpha-gal, a sugar on the surface of cells that can cause immediate rejection of a porcine organ when transplanted into the human body, has been inactivated in the pig’s genome.

“Today marks an exciting moment for United Therapeutics and for the field of xenotransplantation. EXTEND is the second clinical trial in our xeno-organ manufacturing program, and it reflects years of investment in the science, facilities, and regulatory groundwork needed to bring this technology from possibility to clinical reality,” said Jayme Locke, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer, Xenotransplantation at United Therapeutics.

“We are demonstrating that an investigational manufactured organ program can move methodically from the laboratory to patients, always with patient safety first. We are deeply grateful to the participant, their family, and the NYU Langone team,” said Leigh Peterson, Ph.D., Executive Vice President, Product Development & Xenotransplantation at United Therapeutics.

“Every day, people with kidney failure die waiting for an organ that never comes. The need for new sources of organs is urgent. UThymoKidney is designed with the intention to help a recipient’s immune system accept the organ and reduce the risk of organ rejection. The EXTEND study provides a carefully designed, scientifically rigorous way to determine whether another approach to xenotransplantation can deliver real benefit to patients who have few other options,” said Robert Montgomery, M.D., D.Phil., the H. Leon Pachter, M.D., Professor of Surgery; Chair of the Department of Surgery at NYU Grossman School of Medicine; and Director of the NYU Langone Transplant Institute, who led the transplant team that performed the first xenotransplant in the EXTEND study.

About United Therapeutics’ Xenotransplantation Program

United Therapeutics is advancing clinical trials called EXTEND, EXPAND, and EXPRESS, which are intended to support Biologics License Applications (BLA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for each of its three investigational xenotransplantation products:

EXTEND (NCT07224763) is a multicenter, open-label, combination phase 1/2/3 clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of UThymoKidney. This phaseless trial will progress without separate phase 1, 2, and 3 studies typically associated with conventional drug approvals.

Study participants will receive a UThymoKidney transplant followed by a 24-week post-transplant follow-up period, including the evaluation of all study endpoints and safety assessments. After the 24-week post-transplant follow-up period, participants who receive a UThymoKidney will continue to be followed for the rest of their lives, including monitoring for UThymoKidney function and zoonotic infections.

Efficacy endpoints include participant survival rate, UThymoKidney survival rate, change in measured glomerular filtration rate1, donor specific hyporesponsiveness2, and change in quality of life3 in participants at 24 weeks post-transplant, as well as overall survival time of participants receiving a UThymoKidney and overall survival time of the UThymoKidney post-transplant. Safety endpoints include the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, all-cause mortality, and the incidence of proteinuria4, zoonotic infections, and opportunistic infections5.

The first six transplants will take place at two centers, with a 12-week waiting period between the first and second transplants. After all six participants reach at least 12 weeks post-transplant, safety and efficacy data will be reviewed by an Independent Data Monitoring Committee to determine if the study should continue. United Therapeutics intends to present the data from the first six transplants to the FDA for review prior to including additional transplant centers and increasing the study sample size to support a BLA. Additional details on the EXTEND study, including full inclusion and exclusion criteria, are available at ClinicalTrials.gov.

EXPAND (NCT06878560) is a multicenter, open-label, safety and efficacy study of United Therapeutics’ UKidney™ in patients with ESRD. The EXPAND study is currently being conducted at NYU Langone Health and Northwestern Medicine, with the potential to include other centers if initial data are supportive. EXPAND is the world’s first clinical trial designed specifically to generate the definitive safety and efficacy data needed to support an application for regulatory approval (i.e., a registration study).

EXPRESS is an open-label, safety and efficacy study of United Therapeutics’ UHeart™ in patients with advanced heart failure. It will start at a single center with potential to include other centers if initial data are supportive.

The UThymoKidney is a xenokidney that contains porcine thymic tissue and is derived from a pig with a single gene edit.

The UKidney and UHeart are derived from a pig with 10 gene edits. Six human genes are added to the pig genome to facilitate immunological acceptance and compatibility of the organ in the human recipient. Four porcine genes are inactivated or “knocked out” to reduce the risk of organ rejection and to moderate organ growth.

United Therapeutics' xeno-organs are all investigational-stage products which have not been approved in any jurisdiction for any indication.

The Organ Shortage Crisis and ESRD

Demand for organ transplants far exceeds the supply of available organs, and alternative organ sources are needed. In the United States alone, there are approximately 830,000 patients with kidney failure, over 550,000 patients on dialysis, and more than 90,000 patients on the kidney transplant waiting list. Only about 22,000 deceased donor kidney transplants occurred in 20256. The 2024 US Renal Data System Annual Report found that, three years after starting dialysis, only 12% of patients had been placed on an OPTN kidney transplant waitlist and more than 40% had died without receiving a kidney transplant7. Xenotransplantation offers the potential to mitigate, and perhaps even solve, the organ shortage crisis.

About United Therapeutics

Founded by CEO Martine Rothblatt to discover a cure for her daughter's life-threatening rare disease, pulmonary arterial hypertension, United Therapeutics transforms the treatment of rare diseases and pioneers alternatives to expand the supply of transplantable organs. From our innovative therapies to our groundbreaking manufactured organs, we are bold and unconventional. We move quickly from scientific theory to practical technologies that can save lives. As a public benefit corporation, even our legal structure reflects our commitments. We serve patients, act with integrity, create long-term shareholder value, and operate with sustainable practices that protect the future we are working to build. Key Terms

esrdmedical
End-stage renal disease (ESRD) is the final, irreversible stage of chronic kidney failure when the kidneys can no longer sustain the body's fluid, electrolyte and waste balance on their own. It is typically defined clinically by very low kidney function (often an estimated glomerular filtration rate below about 15 mL/min/1.73 m²) or by the need for long-term renal replacement therapy such as dialysis or kidney transplantation. ESRD describes a medical state, not a specific diagnosis or treatment, and signals that ongoing dialysis or a transplant will be required to replace lost kidney function.
xenotransplantationmedical
Transplanting organs, tissues, or cells from one species into a human, most often using genetically modified animals as donors. Investors watch this area because successful xenotransplantation could create large new markets for treating organ failure but also faces steep scientific, regulatory, ethical and reimbursement hurdles—think of fitting a part from a different-model car: if it works it can extend life and value, but compatibility and approval risks are high.
allogeneic kidney transplantationmedical
Surgical replacement of a failing kidney using a kidney donated by another person whose tissue is not genetically identical to the recipient; the donor can be living or deceased. Successful allogeneic transplantation requires blood‑type and tissue‑matching tests and ongoing immunosuppressive drugs to prevent the recipient’s immune system from rejecting the graft, which creates long‑term tradeoffs such as infection risk and the possibility of chronic rejection. It is distinct from autologous transplantation (using the patient’s own tissue) and syngeneic transplantation (from an identical twin).
open-labeltechnical
Open-label describes a situation where everyone involved in a study or process knows the full details, such as who is receiving a treatment or intervention. For investors, understanding whether a project or product is open-label helps gauge the level of transparency and potential biases, influencing trust and decision-making. It’s like knowing whether a test or experiment is conducted openly or behind closed doors.
biologics license applicationsregulatory
A biologics license application is a formal request submitted to a regulatory agency to get permission to market a biological medicine—such as vaccines, blood products, or gene and cell therapies—after clinical testing. It’s like applying for a safety and quality permit that lets a company sell a complex medical product; investors watch its progress because approval clears the way for revenue while rejection or delays create significant financial risk.
zoonotic infectionsmedical
Zoonotic infections are illnesses that jump from animals to people, caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites that normally live in nonhuman hosts. They matter to investors because outbreaks can quickly change demand for medical products, disrupt agriculture, travel and supply chains, and trigger new regulations or vaccine and testing spending—similar to a fire in one building that forces nearby businesses to change how they operate and spend.

Just in Time for Holiday Shopping & Consigning

The RealReal's third LA store offers personalized luxury consignment services, expert valuations and a constantly evolving assortment of one-of-one designer fashion, handbags, jewelry and watches

GLENDALE, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The RealReal (Nasdaq: REAL), the world's largest online marketplace for authenticated luxury resale, today announced the official opening of its newest Los Angeles-area store at The Americana at Brand located at 230 S Brand Blvd in Glendale, California. The location expands The RealReal's Southern California presence, bringing its full-service luxury consignment and shopping experience to one of the region's premier shopping destinations.

The Glendale store offers customers the opportunity to shop and consign authenticated luxury in one location, with a curated, constantly evolving assortment of designer fashion, handbags, fine jewelry, watches and accessories. Shoppers can discover one-of-one pieces from sought-after luxury houses including Chanel, Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Dior, Gucci, The Row, Cartier and Rolex, while consignors can meet with luxury experts to learn more about the value of items in their closets.

"Glendale is a natural fit for The RealReal, with a community that appreciates great style, quality craftsmanship and the value of luxury," said Rati Sahi Levesque, President & CEO, The RealReal. "We wanted to make it incredibly easy for customers in Glendale and surrounding communities to give the pieces they no longer wear a second life. Our trained in-store experts handle the entire consignment process. And, we have a constantly changing assortment of one-of-a-kind luxury pieces, so there's something new to discover with every visit!"

The opening comes as consumers increasingly embrace resale as an integral part of luxury shopping. According to The RealReal's 2026 Resale Report, demand for vintage has increased 432% since 2020, while searches for 2000s fashion have risen 93% year over year. More than half of The RealReal's customer base is now Gen Z and Millennials, reflecting a growing appetite for unique pieces, fashion history and individual expression.

The Glendale store offers:

  • Personalized Consignment Services: One-on-one consultations with luxury experts to help customers sell designer fashion, handbags, fine jewelry, watches and accessories.
  • Luxury Expertise & Valuations: Expert evaluations and insights into resale value and market demand.
  • Curated Luxury Shopping: A regularly refreshed assortment of authenticated, one-of-one pieces spanning iconic designers, vintage fashion and hard-to-find luxury.
  • Private Luxury Appointments: Personalized appointments for customers interested in exceptional fine jewelry, watches, rare handbags and other high-value pieces.
  • Special Offer: $100 credit to shop in-store when you consign at least one accepted item. Site credit is valid in-store, same-day only. Ask store associates for details.

The new store joins The RealReal's existing Southern California locations on Melrose Avenue and in Brentwood, Los Angeles, as well as Newport Beach, further expanding access to authenticated luxury resale and personalized consignment services across the region.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hotel101 Global Holdings Corp. (NASDAQ Ticker: HBNB) (“Hotel101” or “Hotel101 Global”), a leading asset-light, prop-tech hospitality platform pioneering a globally standardized “condotel” business model, listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange and a subsidiary of Philippine-listed DoubleDragon Corporation (PSE Ticker: DD), announces the signing of definitive binding agreements for the development of an approx. 606-room Hotel101-Johor Bahru, Malaysia.

Hotel101 Global Team believes it ensures all its projects via direct developments, joint ventures and licensing to local developers in various countries worldwide are in prime and strategic locations.

The project situated at the Flagship A of Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ). JS-SEZ is a cross-border economic partnership between Malaysia and Singapore, established via bilateral agreement in January 2025, that pairs Johor's land, resources, and cost-competitive manufacturing capacity with Singapore's capital, financial services, and global connectivity. Spanning roughly 3,500 square kilometers across southern Johor with flagship zones and promoted sectors ranging from digital economy, manufacturing, and logistics to green energy and services, the zone offers tailored incentives, streamlined approvals, and improved cross-border movement to attract high-value investment and create skilled jobs.

The hotel, to be named Hotel101-Johor Bahru, is planned to occupy a prime site on the corner of Jalan Tun Abdul Razak and the Johor Bahru Inner Ring Road in the heart of Johor Bahru’s central business district. This strategic position is expected to offer guests excellent connectivity, sitting only around two minutes from the Bukit Chagar RTS Link Station—the key Malaysian hub of the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link that is expected to connect directly to Woodlands North in Singapore in around five minutes. The area has rapidly emerged as one of Johor’s key growth districts, known for its modern infrastructure, improving transport links, and strong mix of residential, commercial, and tourism developments, while sitting at the centre of one of the world’s busiest land border crossings.

Upon completion, guests are expected to benefit from outstanding road connectivity and proximity to the upcoming RTS Link.

  • Proximity to Major Attractions and Connectivity: Situated within the Johor Bahru CBD that is expected to be served by the upcoming RTS Link, JB Sentral, major shopping malls, and the wider cross-border market. The site is expected to offer a balance of modern urban development and strong cross-border demand, with easy access to key commercial amenities, residential communities, and the reported 430,000–450,000 daily travellers moving between Malaysia and Singapore.

When completed, Hotel101-Johor Bahru is expected to generate approx. MYR275.73 million (US$66.78 million) in sales revenue once fully sold and is expected to be the largest hotel by room count in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, forming part of Hotel101 Global’s global expansion strategy.

Hotel101-Johor Bahru is expected to offer 4-star amenities at affordable prices, including a ballroom, ample meeting spaces, and a conference center tailored for business events. Consistent with Hotel101’s offerings across its locations globally, guests are expected to enjoy modern rooms, 24/7 reception, all-day dining, swimming pools, a full-size gym, a business center, children’s playground, ample parking, luggage storage, and other amenities.

The development is subject to customary governmental, regulatory, corporate and other approvals.

Listed on Nasdaq (Ticker: HBNB) with a market capitalization of approx. Hotel101 aims to disrupt the global hotel and hospitality sector through its unique tech-enabled business model that positions it to generate revenues twice: first from the advance sale of individual hotel units during the construction phase; and second, from long-term recurring revenue derived from day-to-day hotel operations. The expansion of Hotel101 toward its long-term goal to operate in 100 countries globally is expected to be driven mainly by joint ventures and, in the future, license agreements with local developers in various countries worldwide.

The Hotel101 Global Group is advancing its global expansion plans toward its medium-term goal to be in 25 countries and its long-term goal of operating one million Hotel101 rooms in 100 countries globally.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Intrepid Metals Corp. More than 3,100 metres of drilling have been completed in seven step-out holes, and the Company's geophysics survey is nearing completion to support upcoming tests of deeper carbonate replacement deposit ("CRD") and porphyry copper targets. Ivanhoe Electric Inc.'s ("Ivanhoe Electric") recently announced copper-gold discovery at its adjacent Gleeson Copper Project ("Gleeson"), immediately west of Corral, further highlights the district's exploration potential (please refer to Ivanhoe Electric's news release dated November 19, 2026)1,2.

"The Intrepid team continues to make steady progress at Corral, with over 3,100 metres completed in 7 step-out drill holes at the Holliday and Ringo Zones," said Matt Lennox-King, Chairman and Interim CEO of Intrepid. "The extensive IP & MT survey is nearing completion and will be a key targeting tool as we progress through the remaining ~7,000 metres of the drill program at Corral. As the program progresses, we will be testing new deeper CRD targets and porphyry copper targets for the first time."

"We would also like to congratulate our neighbour, Ivanhoe Electric, on their Gleeson copper-gold discovery announced yesterday, which we view as a game changer for the wider district," continued Mr. Lennox-King. "The Gleeson discovery is located just roughly 150 metres west of our Project boundary and reportedly bears strong similarities in copper and gold grades, host rocks and geologic setting to our Holliday, Earp, Ringo and Clanton Zones. Our Curly Porphyry Target (please refer to Intrepid's news release dated July 14, 2026 titled "Intrepid Metals Identifies New Porphyry Target at Corral Copper" for details about the Curly Target) sits immediately east of Ivanhoe Electric's Gleeson discovery drill holes and we look forward to drilling at Curly as part of the current program."

Exploration Highlights:

  • Drilling: Approximately 3,100 metres of step-out drilling has been completed at the Holliday and Ringo Zones in 7 drill holes targeting extensions to the previously drilled high-grade copper gold mineralization.

  • Geophysics: The induced polarization ("IP") and Magnetotelluric ("MT") survey which began in mid-September is nearing completion. The survey covers the northern 75% of the Project and the results of the survey will be a key targeting tool for the remainder of the program.

  • Surface Work Defines New Targets: Ongoing geological mapping, rock and soil sampling, and portable X-ray fluorescence ("pXRF") analysis of fracture-fill material have helped define and advance key new target areas including Curly, Kate, and Mattie, each of which is a priority area for drilling.

This process produces high quality, low cost, scalable, 'tuneable' and low/no contaminant graphene suitable for use in clean-technology and other applications.

“Our third quarter results reflect a challenging U.S. sugar market,” said Jonathan Taylor, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Sucro. “Sugar prices were lower, and customs duties, tariffs and a sharp increase in diesel fuel prices and carrier surcharges added cost to the sugar we delivered in the U.S. Competitive market conditions meant we were not able to pass these additional costs on to our customers, and that weighed on our refining margins. Even so, we held adjusted gross profit essentially flat year-over-year and delivered a third consecutive record quarter for refinery volumes, which speaks to the resilience of our integrated model.”

“The investments we have made in our refineries leave Sucro well positioned for 2027,” Mr. Taylor continued. “Our new Hamilton refinery is operating and steadily improving, following the consolidation of our Canadian production into that single state-of-the-art facility. University Park is now a full refinery, and together with Lackawanna it is prepared to deliver significant volumes of higher value-added organic sugar in 2027. We have also begun renegotiating delivery terms with customers to recover higher freight costs. With this expanded and more flexible refining capacity in place, we believe Sucro is ready to benefit as market conditions become more favorable in 2027.”

Results from Operations – Three Months Ended September 30, 2026

Revenue for the quarter was $126.8 million (compared to $132.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025), with sugar deliveries of 147,428 metric tons (compared to 147,853 metric tons for the corresponding period in 2025). The decrease in revenue was mainly driven by lower average sugar delivery prices of $843.50 per metric ton, compared to $893.30 per metric ton in the prior-year period, reflecting market conditions. Adjusted gross profit was $13.1 million (compared to $13.4 million for the corresponding period in 2025), representing an adjusted gross profit margin of 10.3% (compared to 10.1% for the corresponding period in 2025). Adjusted gross profit per metric ton delivered was $88.78 (compared to $90.91 for the corresponding period in 2025).

Net income for the quarter was $18.5 million (compared to $15.4 million for the corresponding period in 2025). EBITDA was $27.2 million (compared to $20.8 million for the corresponding prior period), and Adjusted EBITDA was $7.0 million (compared to $8.1 million for the corresponding prior period), with an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 5.5% compared to 6.1% for the corresponding prior period. The decrease in Adjusted EBITDA reflects higher selling, general and administrative expenses, including the $1.6 million inventory provision noted above under “Financial Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026”.

U.S. market conditions weighed on margins during the quarter. Logistics and freight costs increased to $22.5 million from $14.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven predominantly by customs duties and tariffs and by higher delivery freight costs, as diesel fuel prices and related carrier fuel surcharges rose substantially in the second half of 2026. Competitive dynamics in the U.S. market limited the Company’s ability to pass these additional costs on to customers, compressing margins on certain sales. Refinery adjusted gross profit per metric ton declined to $82.45 from $187.66 in the prior-year period, which also reflects additional transportation costs associated with transferring product between facilities during the commissioning and ramp-up of the University Park refinery. During the third quarter, the Company began renegotiating delivery terms with customers to recover these additional costs.

Sucro’s refineries delivered a record 105,614 metric tons in the quarter, nearly double the 53,873 metric tons delivered in the corresponding period of 2025, and 301,919 metric tons year to date, an increase of 87.4%. These volumes reflect the ramp-up of the Company’s new Hamilton, Ontario refinery, export opportunities from Canada, and the conversion of the University Park, Illinois facility into a full refinery that also supplies a related third-party facility in Memphis. In the fourth quarter, the Company expects to decommission its legacy Hamilton refinery and consolidate its Canadian operations into the new state-of-the-art facility, which is expected to improve production and overhead costs per metric ton. The Company has also increased its organic raw sugar inventory in preparation to deliver significant volumes of organic sugar from its Lackawanna and University Park refineries in 2027, strengthening its leadership position in the U.S. organic sugar market.

The Company’s joint venture refinery in Belize, developed with Santander Sugar Limited, is expected to begin operations in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Company has discontinued its Guyana refinery project and terminated its joint venture agreement with GAICO Construction & General Services Inc.

The Company is in the process of refinancing all of its term debt relating to its U.S. facilities, including $17.5 million of loans maturing within the next 12 months, and expects to complete this process before year-end. As of September 30, 2026, the Company was in compliance with the financial covenants under its credit facilities.

Award of Restricted Share Units

The Board of Directors has awarded 18,498 restricted share units (“RSUs”) to non-executive directors as part of their annual retainer under the Company’s Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan. These RSU awards occur semi-annually in April and November of each year. The RSUs awarded will vest one year from the date of the award. All awards are subject to regulatory approval.

Q3 2026 Investor Call

The Company will host a conference call on Friday, November 20, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time during which Jonathan Taylor, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, and Stefano D’Aniello, Chief Financial Officer, will discuss Sucro’s financial performance for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

About Sucro

Sucro is a growth-oriented sugar trader and refiner that operates throughout the Americas, with a primary focus on serving the North American sugar market. The Company operates a highly integrated and interconnected sugar supply business, utilizing the entire sugar supply chain to service its customers. Sucro’s integrated supply chain includes sourcing raw and refined sugar from countries throughout Latin America, and refined sugar from its own refineries, and delivering to customers in North America and the Caribbean. Since its inception in 2014, Sucro has achieved growth by creating value for customers through continuous process innovation and supply chain re-engineering. Sucro has established a broad production, sales, and sourcing network throughout North America with cane sugar refineries in Hamilton, Ontario, Lackawanna, New York, and University Park, Illinois (a suburb of Chicago), additional value-added processing and packaging facilities, and a cane sugar refinery under development in Belize through a joint venture. (NYSE: MTZ) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Murphy Corporation ("Murphy"), one of the largest and most respected mechanical contractors (“the Transaction”) in the United States. Founded in 1907 and continuously family owned and operated for more than 119 years, Murphy has built a scaled, full-service platform providing mechanical, plumbing and process infrastructure solutions across mission-critical end markets. With approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals and national execution capabilities, Murphy serves a diversified portfolio of customers in aviation and defense, healthcare, pharmaceutical manufacturing, technology, food processing, refrigeration and advanced manufacturing, supported by industry-leading engineering, preconstruction and fabrication capabilities. Murphy's experienced management team, led by President and Chief Executive Officer Patrick Murphy, will remain in place following the Transaction.

In addition to its large-scale construction capabilities, Murphy maintains a substantial service and maintenance business providing recurring HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, controls and other mechanical services to mission-critical facilities as well as other market sectors. MasTec believes this business is positioned for significant growth as Murphy expands its owner-direct relationships and supports the increasing number of data centers and other large-load facilities transitioning from construction into ongoing operation. This recurring service revenue complements Murphy’s project-based operations, strengthens customer relationships and enhances the resilience and visibility of its financial performance. For the two years ended March 31, 2026, Murphy delivered strong double-digit growth in both revenue and EBITDA, driven by increasing demand for mission-critical infrastructure, strong customer relationships and consistent execution for its customers. Murphy is projected to generate full calendar year 2026 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $775 million and approximately $140 million, respectively. Murphy will serve as a new operating group of MasTec, and Murphy’s financial results are expected to be reflected in the Clean Energy and Infrastructure Segment.

Jose Mas, MasTec’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, "We are excited to welcome Murphy and its talented team members to the MasTec family. Murphy has built one of the premier integrated mechanical contracting businesses in the United States through exceptional customer service, operational excellence and an unwavering commitment to safety. Just as importantly, Murphy has built a culture that closely aligns with MasTec's values, including a commitment to entrepreneurship, accountability, safety, long-term relationships and taking care of its people.

“Murphy expands MasTec’s capabilities in some of the fastest growing and most diverse infrastructure markets in North America. Its highly skilled union craft workforce, supported by established apprenticeship, training and field-leadership programs, provides the labor capacity and execution expertise required to deliver large, complex projects safely and efficiently. Together, we will be able to provide customers with a broader range of self-perform infrastructure services across both the construction and operational phases of mission-critical facilities.

“We believe Murphy's differentiated market position, strong recurring service and maintenance revenue, attractive margin profile and substantial growth opportunities make it an exceptional strategic fit for MasTec and a highly compelling investment for our shareholders."

Patrick Murphy, President and CEO of Murphy, commented, “For over 100 years, our family has had the privilege of leading a company built by outstanding employees and trusted by exceptional customers. As we considered the future of Murphy, it was important to find a partner that shared our commitment to safety, integrity, operational excellence and enduring relationships.

“We found that partner in the MasTec family. Their reputation for execution, entrepreneurial culture and commitment to investing in people made this a natural fit. By joining MasTec, we will be able to provide additional opportunities for our employees, expand the capabilities we bring to our customers and continue building on the legacy that has defined Murphy for more than a century.

“Most importantly, our customers, employees and partners can expect continuity from the team and culture that have made Murphy successful, while benefiting from the scale and resources of one of North America's leading infrastructure companies.”

Transaction Rationale

Expands MasTec's Participation Across Mission-Critical Infrastructure: Murphy adds leading mechanical, plumbing, HVAC and process infrastructure capabilities serving highly attractive and diverse end markets. Together, MasTec and Murphy will provide a broader range of self-perform infrastructure solutions “inside the fence”.

Adds A Scarce, Scaled Mechanical Infrastructure Platform: Murphy is among the largest mechanical contractors in the United States, with over 100 years of operating history, approximately 1,600 employees, including approximately 1,200 highly skilled union craft professionals, national execution capabilities and one of the most experienced leadership teams in the industry. Opportunities to acquire assets of this scale and quality are infrequent.

Enhances Technical Capabilities and Execution Certainty: Murphy brings differentiated engineering, preconstruction, virtual design, prefabrication capabilities and building information modeling that support project execution, labor productivity, schedule certainty and quality performance. These capabilities create meaningful value for customers and represent significant barriers to entry within the industry.

Highly Complementary Culture and Leadership Team: Murphy's family ownership, people-first culture, commitment to safety and operational excellence closely align with MasTec's values and operating philosophy. The Transaction preserves an experienced leadership team while providing additional resources to support continued growth and long-term customer success.

Deepens Relationships with Leading Infrastructure Customers: Murphy serves a diversified base of blue-chip customers and project partners across critical infrastructure markets, supported by longstanding relationships and a proven track record delivering large, complex projects safely and successfully. The combination creates opportunities to expand services with existing customers and pursue larger opportunities together.

Immediate Financial Contributions with Significant Long-Term Growth Opportunities: Murphy has demonstrated a consistent track record of growth, profitability and cash flow generation supported by strong backlog visibility, recurring service and maintenance revenue and favorable long-term trends across its end markets. MasTec expects meaningful opportunities to expand Murphy’s service business by supporting the growing installed base of operational data centers and other diverse facilities, including facilities where Murphy’s construction relationships and knowledge provide a natural foundation for ongoing maintenance and support. MasTec expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenue, Adjusted EBITDA, earnings per share and cash flow from operations.

Transaction Overview

The purchase price is approximately $1.25 billion payable in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments. Additionally, there is a potential earnout payment based on the cumulative three-year financial performance of Murphy post-closing. MasTec has arranged to finance the Transaction with a bank term loan entered into contemporaneously with the Transaction agreement. MasTec’s September 30, 2026 pro forma net leverage is estimated to be 2.7x with further deleveraging expected to reduce net leverage to less than 2.0x during calendar year 2027. Substantially all conditions to closing have been satisfied and MasTec expects to close the transaction expeditiously.

McDermott Will & Schulte LLP and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP are serving as MasTec's Transaction and financing legal advisors, respectively. Sable Capital, LLC is serving as financial advisor to Murphy, and Holland & Knight LLP as its legal advisor.

About MasTec

MasTec, Inc. is a leading North American infrastructure engineering and construction company focused primarily on engineering, building, installation, maintenance and upgrade of communications, energy and utility and other infrastructure. MasTec primarily operates under four business segments including Communications, serving both wireless and wireline/fiber infrastructure; Power Delivery, serving primarily utility customers in transmission, distribution and large load electrical infrastructure markets; Pipeline Infrastructure serving energy and other customers with installation and maintenance services primarily for natural gas pipeline and distribution infrastructure; and Clean Energy and Infrastructure, providing renewable energy engineering and construction services, as well as for heavy civil and other industrial infrastructure markets. Learn more at www.mastec.com.

About Murphy

Murphy is a premier national contractor designing, constructing, and maintaining mechanical systems for the commercial, industrial, and institutional markets with unique capabilities to manage complex and demanding projects. We continually innovate and improve our business processes to maximize value for our customers and to better our company’s performance. We achieve this through safety excellence, empowerment of our people, effective teamwork, development of our partners, and dedicated customer focus. To learn more, visit www.murphynet.com.

WeRide Inc. Announces Unaudited Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- WeRide Inc. (“WeRide” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: WRD; HKEX: 0800), a global leader in autonomous driving technology, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Operational and Financial Highlights

  • Revenue grew 88.0% and gross margin expanded to 43.0%, driven primarily by the overseas business. Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million), representing an increase of 88.0% year over year and 38.8% quarter over quarter. Gross margin reached 43.0%, up 10.1 percentage points year over year. Revenue from higher-margin overseas operations was RMB146.9 million (US$21.9 million), up 171.5% year over year, and accounted for 45.7% of total revenue.
  • AI Infrastructure revenue nearly doubled, capturing fast-growing data demand from Physical AI. Leveraging the closed‑loop data capabilities built over years of autonomous‑driving operations, Jingshuo Technology, WeRide’s Physical AI Infrastructure (“AI Infrastructure”) subsidiary, serves customers across embodied AI, robotics, autonomous driving and foundation models, with end‑to‑end solutions spanning pre‑training data, post‑training environments and trusted verification. Driven by surging demand for high-quality physical-world data, revenue from this business nearly doubled year over year.
  • Quarterly Robotaxi revenue surpassed RMB100 million; Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics. In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, up 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue. The Company’s Robotaxi operations in Guangzhou achieved positive unit economics, marking an important milestone in validating the economics of Robotaxi operations at scale.
  • Global L4 fleet of approximately 4,100 vehicles; Robotaxi fleet up 26% quarter over quarter. As of October 31, 2026, the Company’s global L4 fleet comprised approximately 4,100 vehicles, including more than 2,300 Robotaxis. The Robotaxi fleet increased by 26% quarter over quarter.
  • WeRide secured Spain’s first national operating permit for L4 autonomous passenger vehicles, accelerating commercialization in Europe. The Company received Spain’s first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the Spanish Directorate-General for Traffic (“DGT”), laying the groundwork for commercial services in Spain. The Company also advanced its operations in Switzerland, Belgium and France, and began road testing in Slovakia, while continuing to expand its collaboration with local public transportation operators.
  • Asset-light expansion accelerating in the Middle East, with a fleet of approximately 600 vehicles. The Company continues to expand its operating fleet and service areas in the Middle East, targeting full coverage of the core urban areas of Abu Dhabi and Dubai by year-end. The Company’s Middle East fleet reached approximately 600 vehicles, up approximately 50% from about 400 vehicles as of July 31, 2026. As of the date of this release, WeRide is Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States, measured by the number of fully driverless Robotaxis operating on its platform.
  • L2++/L3 mass production accelerating, with cumulative WRD 3.0 deliveries exceeding 100,000 units. Now, the AION i60, GAC Trumpchi Yue 7 and AION Ray7, all equipped with the Company’s WRD 3.0 one-stage end-to-end L2++/L3 solution, were launched, extending the solution’s adoption across more production models and driving scenarios. By the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of WRD 3.0 exceeded 100,000 units. The Company continued to expand its partnership network, establishing collaborations with several leading OEM groups.

L4 Business Update

Robotaxi Business Update

In the third quarter of 2026, Robotaxi revenue exceeded RMB100 million for the first time, representing an increase of 204.0% year over year, with overseas markets contributing more than 90% of total Robotaxi revenue.

International Operations

  • Overseas Robotaxi revenue grew rapidly, supported by the Company’s high-margin, asset-light business model. In overseas markets, the Company provides autonomous driving technology and remote assistance, while local partners provide fleet investment and handle other operations. This division of roles enables the Company to continue scaling deployments across Europe and the Middle East with greater capital efficiency.
  • The Middle East fleet expanded, with broader coverage of core urban areas. The Company continued to expand its Middle East fleet to approximately 600 Robotaxis and extend its operating areas in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, now covering the major districts of both cities’ core urban areas. This lays the foundation for broader service coverage and future operational growth.
  • WeRide obtained Spain’s first national L4 autonomous driving permit and advanced its Madrid deployment. In September 2026, the Company, together with Uber and AVOMO, received Spain's first L4 autonomous passenger vehicle operating permit from the DGT, allowing vehicles to be deployed on public roads. The permit authorizes testing of WeRide’s GXR autonomous vehicles in Spain and marks the beginning of mapping in the Madrid region ahead of the Company’s first joint launch in Europe.
  • L4 deployments and services in Switzerland and Slovakia continued to advance. Along with its partners, Schweizerische Bundesbahnen (“SBB”) and Swiss Transit Lab (“STL”), the Company launched public Robotaxi services in Canton of Zurich. In Slovakia, the first batch of Robotaxis began road testing, building operating experience to support future deployments.
  • Robotaxi services in Asia continued to expand. In Singapore, the Company continued to expand its Robotaxi service together with Grab and had provided more than 20,000 L4 autonomous driving rides as of the end of the third quarter of 2026.

China Operations

  • Guangzhou operations achieved positive unit economics, with further improvements in operational efficiency. In the third quarter of 2026, domestic Robotaxi operations achieved an average of 21 daily orders per vehicle, with a peak of 33 orders per vehicle in one day. Cumulative registered users continued to grow rapidly, up 143.5% from the end of the previous quarter.
  • Service areas in key cities continued to expand. In Guangzhou, the Company’s Robotaxi service covers Tianhe, Haizhu and the core districts of Huangpu. These developments provide a solid foundation for further scaling the Company’s Robotaxi business.

Other L4 Business Updates

  • Robobus achieved one of Europe’s first fully driverless services. At Zurich Airport, the Company’s Robobus now operates without an onboard safety operator, making it one of the first fully driverless Robobus services in Europe. The Company is also advancing autonomous driving collaborations with public transportation operators such as Keolis in France and expanding its Robobus operations in Belgium. In Slovakia, the Robobus fleet has arrived and commenced testing.
  • Robosweeper expanded its presence in Singapore. The Company has partnered with leading environmental services providers, Chye Thiam Maintenance and RE Sustainability, to deliver sanitation services across key locations including Marina Coastal Drive, the Esplanade and Sentosa Island, with further deployments expected in the near term.

L2++/L3 Business Update

  • Cumulative deliveries exceeded 100,000 units, with a growing mass-production pipeline. As of the end of the quarter, cumulative deliveries of the Company’s WRD 3.0 L2++/L3 solution exceeded 100,000 units. During the quarter, the Company secured 10 new L2++/L3 mass-production design wins, further expanding its pipeline of future production programs.
  • Customer base and design-win portfolio continued to expand. The Company secured multiple new design wins from several leading OEMs, further validating the competitiveness of its technology and expanding its customer reach.
  • The Company’s L2++/L3 solution continued to demonstrate its capabilities in driving competitions. Customer vehicles equipped with the Company’s L2++/L3 solution have won eight championships in the China Intelligent Driving Competition, further demonstrating the solution’s overall technical capabilities.

AI Infrastructure Business Update

High-quality real-world data and verifiable training environments are key enablers for the development of Physical AI foundation models.

  • End-to-end capabilities covering the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Building on the closed-loop data capabilities developed through the Company’s autonomous driving operations, Jingshuo provides pre-training data, post-training environments and trusted verification across the full path from pre-training to continuous learning. Its capabilities span data collection, quality control and annotation, synthetic data generation, environment construction, independent evaluation and post-training integration. It offers high-quality datasets, licensing of data-processing software and post-training environments, and customized data services to customers in autonomous driving, foundation models, embodied AI and robotics.
  • A three-layer product suite and two engines, closing the “collection–assetization–training” loop.  Jingshuo’s product stack comprises three layers. EGOK is a proprietary wearable multimodal collection terminal with hardware-level synchronization. SkillForge turns first-person operation data into trainable, verifiable and licensable skill assets with task definitions and success criteria. Crucible is an environment hub that connects tasks into executable, independently judged environments and supports post-training integration. Two engines connect the layers: the Data Engine turns experience into versioned data and skills, and the World Engine, powered by the GENESIS-Robotics world model, turns real-world demonstrations into verifiable training environments.
  • High-quality multimodal data assets support applications across diverse real-world scenarios. Through automated 3D reconstruction, multimodal alignment and fine-grained annotation, Jingshuo has built a large-scale dataset library serving foundation model, embodied AI and robotics customers in China and overseas.

Management Commentary

Tony Han, WeRide’s Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “This quarter showed that our global strategy is working. Overseas markets now generate nearly half of our total revenue and more than 90% of our Robotaxi revenue. Operating driverless fleets in foreign markets is challenging, which is exactly why it is becoming our long-term moat. With new deployments in Europe and a Middle East fleet of approximately 600 vehicles, WeRide is now Uber’s largest autonomous vehicle partner outside the United States by driverless fleet size. In China, our Guangzhou Robotaxi operations achieved positive unit economics, demonstrating that Robotaxi can be a sustainable business. Robotaxi is our core business and the fastest path to commercializing Physical AI. The technology and closed-loop data we have built on real roads now power three mutually reinforcing businesses: Robotaxi, L2++/L3 solutions, and AI Infrastructure, which extends these capabilities to foundation models, embodied AI and robotics. As an infrastructure builder for Physical AI, we are just getting started.”

Jennifer Li, WeRide’s Chief Financial Officer and Head of International, added, “This quarter, revenue grew by 88% to RMB321.5 million, gross margin reached 43%, and overseas revenue made up nearly half of the total. Our asset-light model enables us to expand quickly and efficiently. Based on our operating plan, we have more than four years of cash runway, sufficient to fully fund our path to self-sustaining cash flow. More importantly, we are building a long-term moat. Operating across 13 countries and holding permits in 9 requires years of regulatory trust and operational experience — this is hard to replicate. We will translate this lead into sustainable, profitable growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenue

Total revenue grew 88.0% year over year to RMB321.5 million (US$48.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB171.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the expansion of the Company’s Robotaxi-centered L4 business, rapid growth in the L2++/L3 business and continued growth in the AI Infrastructure business.

Cost of Revenue

Cost of revenue was RMB183.4 million (US$27.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB114.7 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in cost of revenue was in line with revenue growth in the Robotaxi-centered L4 business and the AI Infrastructure business.

Gross Profit and Gross Margin

Gross profit was RMB138.1 million (US$20.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB56.3 million in the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 43.0% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 32.9% in the same period of 2025. Gross margin expansion was mainly driven by revenue growth in the high-margin overseas business and the L2++/L3 business.

Operating Expenses

Operating expenses were RMB505.7 million (US$75.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB435.8 million in the same period of 2025.

  • R&D expenses were RMB465.3 million (US$69.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB316.4 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily due to the increase in personnel and outsourcing labor costs, outsourced R&D expenses and cloud service fees. In addition, from July 1, 2026, the estimated useful lives of IDC-related equipment were uniformly extended to six years, resulting in lower depreciation and amortization expenses.
     
  • Administrative expenses were RMB13.9 million (US$2.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB100.4 million in the same period of 2025. The significant decrease in administrative expenses was primarily due to a reversal of share-based compensation expenses resulting from employee departures, and a decrease in professional service fees, as the same period of 2025 included fees related to the global offering.
     
  • Selling expenses were RMB26.5 million (US$4.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB19.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in selling expenses was primarily due to the increase in sales personnel costs.

Loss for the Period

  • Loss for the period was RMB310.0 million (US$46.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB307.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-IFRS adjusted loss1 for the period was RMB336.5 million (US$50.2 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB275.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (“EBITDA”)2

EBITDA was negative RMB246.4 million (US$36.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, an improvement of 2.9% from negative RMB253.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Loss per Ordinary Share and per ADS3  

  • Basic and diluted loss per ordinary share was RMB0.32 (US$0.05) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.34 in the same period of 2025.
     
  • Basic and diluted loss per ADS was RMB0.96 (US$0.15) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB1.02 in the same period of 2025.

Use of Non-IFRS Financial Measures

In evaluating its business, the Company considers and uses the non-IFRS financial measures of (i) adjusted loss for the period and (ii) EBITDA as supplemental measures to review and assess operating performance. The Company believes that adjusted loss for the period and EBITDA provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating the Company’s consolidated results of operations in the same manner as it helps the Company’s management. HONG KONG, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nano Labs Ltd (“we,” the “Company” or “Nano Labs”), a leading Web 3.0 infrastructure and product solution provider, and a crypto treasury company, today announced that its 2026 annual general meeting of shareholders (the “2026 Annual Meeting”), originally scheduled to be held at 10:00 A.M. on November 24, 2026, Beijing time (9:00 P.M. on November 23, 2026, U.S. Eastern time), has been postponed and will now be held at 10:00 A.M. on December 17, 2026, Beijing time (9:00 P.M. on December 16, 2026, U.S. Eastern time) (the “Postponed Annual Meeting”).

The Postponed Annual Meeting will be held at the same venue as originally scheduled, being 12F, China Yuangu Hanggang Technology Building, 509 Qianjiang Road, Shangcheng District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, 310000, People’s Republic of China.

Postponement of the 2026 Annual Meeting

In determining to postpone the 2026 Annual Meeting, the Board of Directors of the Company (the “Board”) has considered the interests and views of the Company’s shareholders and the importance of providing shareholders with sufficient time and opportunity to review and consider the proposals to be presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting. The Company believes that allowing additional time will facilitate shareholders’ informed consideration of the matters to be submitted for approval and enable them to participate more fully in the voting process. The Company remains committed to respecting the views and interests of its shareholders and facilitating their meaningful and informed participation in the Company’s corporate governance matters.

Record Date and Meeting Proposals

The record date for determining shareholders entitled to receive notice of, and to vote at, the 2026 Annual Meeting remains October 16, 2026, Eastern time (the “Record Date”), unchanged from the original Notice of Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (the “Original Notice”).

The proposals to be considered at the Postponed Annual Meeting remain unchanged from those previously announced. The matters to be considered and voted upon at the Postponed Annual Meeting include:

Share Consolidation and Share Re-designation. To authorize (a) a consolidation of every ten (10) shares with a par value of US$0.002 each in the Company’s issued and unissued share capital into one (1) share with a par value of US$0.02 each (the “Share Consolidation”), and (b) immediately following the Share Consolidation, the re-designation of certain undesignated shares as Class A ordinary shares and Class B ordinary shares (the “Share Re-designation”), subject to the applicable price-based trigger, timing requirements and other conditions set forth in the Original Notice;

Share Sub-division. To authorize a sub-division of every one (1) share with a par value of US$0.002 each in the Company’s issued and unissued share capital into ten (10) shares with a par value of US$0.0002 each (the “Share Sub-division”), subject to the condition that the closing price of the Company’s ordinary shares on the primary stock exchange exceeds US$100.00 per share for a consecutive period of 30 trading days (or such other period as the Board may determine), and the other conditions set forth in the Original Notice; and

Appointment of Independent Auditor. To approve the appointment of MaloneBailey, LLP as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026.

The foregoing descriptions of the proposals are summaries only and are qualified in their entirety by the full text of the resolutions set forth in the Original Notice. Except for the postponement of the 2026 Annual Meeting and the corresponding extension of the deadline for submission of proxy forms, the proposals to be considered at the Postponed Annual Meeting remain unchanged.

Notice of Annual General Meeting and Proxy Materials

On October 13, 2026, the Company furnished its Notice of Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and the form of proxy for shareholders (the “Original Form of Proxy,” and together with the Original Notice, the “Original AGM Materials”) as Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3, respectively, to its Report of Foreign Private Issuer on Form 6-K furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). The Original AGM Materials are also available on the Company’s investor relations website.

In connection with the postponement of the 2026 Annual Meeting, this announcement supplements the Original AGM Materials solely with respect to the rescheduled date and time of the 2026 Annual Meeting and the corresponding extension of the deadline for submission of proxy forms.

For purposes of the Postponed Annual Meeting, all references in the Original AGM Materials to the 2026 Annual Meeting being held on November 24, 2026 (Beijing time) (November 23, 2026, U.S. Eastern time) shall be read as references to December 17, 2026 (Beijing time) (December 16, 2026, U.S. Eastern time), as applicable. Similarly, the original deadline of November 20, 2026 for submission of proxy forms specified in the Original AGM Materials is hereby extended to the close of business on December 14, 2026 (Beijing time). Any references in the Original AGM Materials to the original meeting date, time or proxy submission deadline shall be interpreted accordingly.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Original Form of Proxy, when read together with this announcement, is intended to be used in connection with the Postponed Annual Meeting. References therein to the AGM at the originally scheduled date and time and any adjournment of the AGM shall be interpreted in light of the postponement and the updated meeting date, time and arrangements set forth in this announcement.

Except as expressly supplemented by this announcement, all other information, terms and provisions set forth in the Original AGM Materials remain unchanged and continue to apply to the Postponed Annual Meeting. In the event of any inconsistency between this announcement and the Original AGM Materials with respect to the rescheduled meeting date, time or proxy submission deadline, this announcement shall prevail.

The Company will provide written notice of the postponement to shareholders in accordance with the Company’s memorandum and articles of association. Shareholders are encouraged to review this announcement together with the Original AGM Materials and to submit their completed forms of proxy in accordance with the instructions set forth in the Original Form of Proxy, as supplemented by this announcement, no later than the revised deadline specified above.

The Company appreciates the continued attention, understanding and participation of its shareholders and looks forward to welcoming them to the Postponed Annual Meeting.

About Nano Labs Ltd

Nano Labs Ltd is a leading Web 3.0 infrastructure and product solution provider, and crypto treasury company. Nano Labs is committed to the development of high throughput computing (“HTC”) chips and high performance computing (“HPC”) chips. Nano Labs has built a comprehensive flow processing unit (“FPU”) architecture which offers solution that integrates the features of both HTC and HPC. In addition, Nano Labs has actively positioned itself in the crypto assets space, adopting BNB as its primary reserve asset. It has reserved in mainstream cryptocurrency, BNB, and established an integrated platform covering multiple business verticals, including HTC solutions, HPC solutions and iPollo Claw*. Eurodam's first Asia season features new destinations, more time ashore and opportunities to experience Japan during its famed cherry blossom season

Key Takeaways:

  • Eurodam makes its Asia debut with five new ports, expanding Holland America Line's 2028-2029 season across Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.
  • More time ashore and Japan's cherry blossom season deepen the destination experience, with overnight stays and late-night departures across 14 ports, plus spring sailings timed to give guests opportunities to see the famed blooms.
  • A new 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage expands longer exploration of the region, visiting 13 ports across seven countries and bringing Asia's culinary traditions on board through destination-inspired experiences.

SEATTLE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Holland America Line announced its 2028-2029 Asia cruise season, adding five new ports across Japan, Taiwan, Brunei and the Philippines to a wide-ranging collection of cruises throughout the region. Aboard Eurodam, making its Asia debut, cruises explore Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.

Five new ports, more time ashore and Japan's cherry blossoms highlight Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia season.

Sailing from September 2028 through May 2029, the season features itineraries ranging from 11 to 27 days, with departures from Tokyo, Japan; Hong Kong, China; and Singapore. Standout cruises range from in-depth explorations of Japan to journeys connecting the major cities and islands of Southeast Asia, with 14 overnight ports adding extra time ashore.

"Asia is one of those regions where you can experience something completely different from one port to the next, from a major city like Hong Kong to our new call at Coron in the Philippines, known for its turquoise waters and rich history," said Paul Grigsby, vice president of deployment and revenue planning for Holland America Line. "That contrast is what makes these itineraries so interesting to build. The new ports take guests beyond the places they may already know, introducing them to islands, coastlines and historic communities that reveal another side of the region, while natural phenomena like Japan's cherry blossoms can make the experience completely different depending on when you visit."

The five new ports add a mix of tropical landscapes, natural wonders and historic sites to the season.

  • Coron, Busuanga Island, Philippines, is known for the emerald Twin Lagoons.
  • Japan offers two new locales: Hirara introduces guests to the white-sand beaches and turquoise waters of Miyako Island, while Wakayama offers access to Wakayama Castle and the sacred mountain temples of Koyasan.
  • Magong showcases the striking basalt coastline of Taiwan's Penghu Island.
  • Muara provides a gateway to Brunei Darussalam and the gold-domed Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque.

Spring brings another reason to explore Japan as the country's famed cherry blossom season unfolds across different regions. Guests sailing spring itineraries can seek out the blooms along their journey, while those embarking in Tokyo can extend their stay before or after their cruise for more time to experience the season ashore. Shore excursions provide additional opportunities to take in the seasonal color, including from Kobe, where guests can visit UNESCO World Heritage-listed Himeji Castle and neighboring Koko-en Garden, known for its cherry blossoms in early spring.

More Time to Explore
Across the 2028-2029 Asia season, guests can enjoy overnight stays and late-night departures in 14 ports throughout the region. The additional time ashore creates a more relaxed pace, with opportunities to experience a city after dark, linger over dinner, revisit a favorite spot or take part in longer excursions. By extending time in port into the evening or the following day, guests can experience more of a destination's local culture, cuisine and nightlife without feeling rushed.

  • Overnight ports throughout Asia include Bali, Indonesia; Halong Bay, Vietnam; Hong Kong, China; Incheon (Seoul), South Korea; Keelung (Taipei), Taiwan; Laem Chabang (Bangkok), Thailand; Manila, Philippines; Hiroshima, Osaka and Maizuru, Japan; Phú Mỹ (Ho Chi Minh City) and Halong Bay, Vietnam; Shanghai, China; and Singapore. New overnight stays for the 2028-2029 season include Keelung and Phú Mỹ.
  • Guests can take advantage of extended stays by watching a sunset in Halong Bay, exploring Manila's historic San Agustin Church or experiencing Shanghai's neon city lights after dark.
  • Late-night departures also give guests additional time in Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Maizuru and Osaka, Japan; Halong Bay, Vietnam; and Shanghai, China.

Coffee, Tea and Spice Take Center Stage on New 27-Day Legendary Voyage
New for 2029, Holland America Line will introduce a 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage aboard Eurodam, departing Jan. 3 roundtrip from Singapore. The itinerary visits 13 ports across seven countries, tracing the region's coffee, tea and spice traditions from Java and Manila to Taiwan and Hong Kong, with overnight calls in Bali, Hong Kong and  Phú Mỹ, the gateway to Ho Chi Minh City. On board, Holland America Line plans to bring the journey to life through regionally inspired tea and coffee experiences.

2028-2029 Asia Season Highlights

  • Circle Japan: 11- and 14-day itineraries sail roundtrip or between Tokyo and Yokohama (Tokyo), exploring ports throughout Japan and South Korea. The 14-day cruises visit up to 10 ports, with select extended calls in Hiroshima; the 11-day April 22, 2029, cruise features an overnight in Maizuru.
  • Japan & South Korea Discovery: Two 14-day cruises explore Japan and South Korea, with an overnight in Incheon (Seoul) and extended calls in Osaka and/or Fukuoka. The 11-day Southern Japan & Jeju Discovery, departing May 3, 2029, adds a call at Jeju.
  • Japan, Taiwan & China: The 14-day Japan & Taiwan cruise departs Nov. 5, 2028, from Tokyo to Hong Kong, with overnights in Osaka and Keelung (Taipei). A 14-day China & Japan Discovery departing Feb. 25, 2029, features overnights in Shanghai and Osaka.
  • Southeast Asia Discovery: The 14-day Nov. 19, 2028, sailing from Hong Kong to Singapore features overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Halong Bay. A 17-day holiday itinerary departs Dec. 17, adding Nha Trang, Vietnam, and Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, along with festive onboard programming.
  • Thailand & Philippines Discovery: The 14-day Dec. 3 sailing from Singapore to Hong Kong features six ports, including overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Manila.
  • North Pacific Crossings: Two cruises connect Asia with the Pacific Northwest: a 13-day Vancouver-to-Tokyo crossing with Ketchikan, Alaska, and scenic cruising through the Inside Passage, and a 14-day Tokyo-to-Seattle crossing featuring Kushiro, Japan, and three Alaska ports.

Guests looking to spend even longer in the region can combine select back-to-back itineraries into Collectors' Voyages, extending their exploration across multiple countries and destinations.

Bringing Asia's Flavors On Board
Holland America Line's Destination Dining program brings the itinerary onboard, with menus inspired by the places guests visit. KEARNEY, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The Buckle, Inc. (NYSE: BKE) announced today that net income for the fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis).

Net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.6 percent to $329.2 million from net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026 increased 0.6 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 13-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales decreased 1.4 percent to $52.2 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $53.0 million for the 13-week fiscal quarter ended November 1, 2025.

Net sales for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 increased 4.3 percent to $937.8 million from net sales of $898.7 million for the prior year 39-week fiscal period ended November 1, 2025. Comparable store net sales for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026 increased 2.5 percent from comparable store net sales for the prior year 39-week period ended November 1, 2025. Online sales increased 1.1 percent to $144.5 million for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026, compared to net sales of $142.9 million for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $48.0 million, or $0.95 per share ($0.94 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $48.7 million, or $0.97 per share ($0.96 per share on a diluted basis) for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

Net income for the 39-week fiscal period ended October 31, 2026 was $139.3 million, or $2.75 per share ($2.73 per share on a diluted basis), compared with net income of $128.9 million, or $2.57 per share ($2.55 per share on a diluted basis) for the 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

Management will hold a live audio webcast at 10:00 a.m. EST today to discuss results for the quarter. About Buckle

Buckle is a specialty retailer focused on delivering exceptional service and style through unforgettable experiences. Headquartered in Kearney, Nebraska, Buckle currently operates 452 retail stores in 42 states, which includes the opening of two new stores located in Round Rock, Texas and Elizabethtown, Kentucky in fiscal November (after the fiscal quarter ended). As of the end of the fiscal quarter, it operated 450 stores in 42 states compared with 442 stores in 42 states at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
